title: Summary Of The Lesson From The Cosmos There Is No God But Allah

questions.question: What main truth is introduced at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The passage introduces the reality that beings in the universe help one another in ways far beyond their own power.

questions.question: In what situation is this co-operation seen among beings?
questions.answer: It is seen while they try to continue their existence, and for living things, their lives and duties, amid constant change.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this co-operation cannot be explained by the beings themselves?
questions.answer: Because the help and coordination go beyond their own ability, awareness, and strength.

questions.question: How are the elements described in relation to living creatures?
questions.answer: They are presented as serving and supporting living beings.

questions.question: How do the clouds function in this chain of help?
questions.answer: They are described as aiding plant life.

questions.question: How does the plant world support the animal world?
questions.answer: Plants provide what animals need for their life and survival.

questions.question: How does the animal world support human beings?
questions.answer: Animals are shown as serving human life and benefit.

questions.question: What example is given to show special care for infants?
questions.answer: The flow of milk to feed a baby is given as a sign of merciful provision.

questions.question: Why is the example of an infant’s nourishment important in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that a helpless being receives what it needs without having the ability to secure it by itself.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how living beings receive their provision?
questions.answer: They receive their needs from places they do not expect and in ways beyond their own capacity.

questions.question: What bodily example is used to show inward co-operation?
questions.answer: Food particles are directed to the body’s cells to renew and support them.

questions.question: What does this broad pattern of assistance point to?
questions.answer: It points to a Lord who governs the universe with mercy, wisdom, and care.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the universe to a palace?
questions.answer: To show that it is managed in an organized, purposeful, and well-run way.

questions.question: How are lifeless things described when they work together?
questions.answer: They are described as acting in an orderly way that looks almost aware and responsive, even though they have no feeling of their own.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the co-operation of inanimate things?
questions.answer: They must be directed by the power and command of a compassionate, wise, and glorious Sustainer.

questions.question: Besides co-operation, what other universal patterns are mentioned as signs?
questions.answer: Balance, preservation, beautification, order, and assigned duties are also mentioned.

questions.question: What range of things is used to show the vastness of balance and preservation?
questions.answer: The passage moves from heavenly bodies down to organs, limbs, and even tiny particles in living bodies.

questions.question: What examples are given for beautification and order?
questions.answer: The heavens, the earth, flowers, star systems, and fruits are all given as examples.

questions.question: What does the assigning of duties to things such as the sun, clouds, and bees suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that each part of creation has a set role under deliberate direction.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the importance of these truths for the cosmos’s testimony?
questions.answer: It says they make up the second wing of the universe’s witness to its Creator.

questions.question: According to the passage, what shared reality appears among created things?
questions.answer: A widespread pattern of mutual assistance appears among them.

questions.question: What are beings trying to preserve while this pattern is taking place?
questions.answer: They are trying to preserve their existence, and living beings are also trying to preserve their lives and carry out their functions.

questions.question: What does the phrase about constant upheaval suggest about the world?
questions.answer: It suggests that the world is always in motion and change, not stable or self-sufficient.

questions.question: How does the passage arrange the examples of help among different levels of creation?
questions.answer: It presents them as a chain, moving from basic physical things to plants, then animals, and finally human beings.

questions.question: What does the image of milk for a baby communicate about divine care?
questions.answer: It shows gentle and immediate mercy for the weakest and most needy.

questions.question: What is significant about provision coming from unexpected places?
questions.answer: It shows that sustenance is being sent intentionally, not merely obtained by the creature’s own effort.

questions.question: How does the nourishment of body cells strengthen the main claim?
questions.answer: It shows that even inside the body there is a directed and purposeful system of support.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says food particles are under the control of the Sustainer?
questions.answer: It means they do not move randomly but are directed toward wise and merciful purposes.

questions.question: What larger attribute is shown by these many examples of support and provision?
questions.answer: They show a caring lordship that manages the whole universe.

questions.question: What does governing the cosmos like a palace imply?
questions.answer: It implies rule, arrangement, purpose, and attentive administration.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress that solid and lifeless things are neither aware nor feeling?
questions.answer: To show that their orderly service cannot come from themselves.

questions.question: If lifeless things still act in ways that benefit others, what must follow?
questions.answer: Their action must come from the command and power of One who knows and wills.

questions.question: How does the passage use very large and very small examples together?
questions.answer: It uses both to show that the same wise rule appears throughout all levels of existence.

questions.question: What is the effect of mentioning both the sky and flowers in the same discussion?
questions.answer: It shows that beauty and design are present in both the vast and the delicate parts of creation.

questions.question: Why are fruits like corn and pomegranates mentioned with cosmic structures?
questions.answer: To show that careful order exists in ordinary earthly things just as it does in massive heavenly systems.

questions.question: What do the examples of the sun, moon, elements, clouds, and bees have in common?
questions.answer: They all illustrate that different creatures and forces are given specific functions.

questions.question: In the passage’s argument, what is the role of this whole section on co-operation?
questions.answer: It provides one major part of the universe’s witness to the existence and qualities of its Sustainer.

questions.question: What central idea ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: The whole passage centers on the universe-wide harmony of things helping one another under divine rule.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the ability of created things in relation to this harmony?
questions.answer: It says the harmony exceeds their own limited ability.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the claim that co-operation goes beyond the capacity of creatures?
questions.answer: It can be inferred that another power is organizing and directing them.

questions.question: What first example is given from the natural world to illustrate this help?
questions.answer: The basic elements are said to support living beings.

questions.question: How do clouds fit into the larger system described?
questions.answer: They play a supporting role for plant life within the wider chain of benefit.

questions.question: What role do plants have in this sequence?
questions.answer: They serve animals by becoming a means for their nourishment and life.

questions.question: What role do animals have in this sequence?
questions.answer: They are shown as a means of support and service for human beings.

questions.question: What does the example of nursing teach about weakness and provision?
questions.answer: It teaches that those who are most helpless can still receive exactly what they need.

questions.question: How does the passage treat sustenance as evidence rather than just a biological fact?
questions.answer: It presents sustenance as a sign of intentional care and management.

questions.question: Why is the movement of nutrients to cells an effective example in this argument?
questions.answer: Because it shows hidden, precise service happening inside living bodies without conscious control by the cells.

questions.question: What kind of divine rule is shown by these outward and inward forms of support?
questions.answer: They show a universal rule marked by mercy and care.

questions.question: Why is the palace comparison useful for understanding the cosmos?
questions.answer: It helps the reader picture the cosmos as something structured, governed, and purposeful.

questions.question: What tension does the passage highlight in speaking about inanimate things?
questions.answer: It points out that they are lifeless and unaware, yet they still act in coordinated ways.

questions.question: How does that tension support the passage’s conclusion?
questions.answer: It strengthens the idea that an all-controlling Sustainer is making them serve one another.

questions.question: What does universal equilibrium add to the argument beyond co-operation?
questions.answer: It shows not only mutual help but also measured proportion and stability throughout creation.

questions.question: What is meant by preservation in this context?
questions.answer: It means the careful maintenance of things in a regular and ongoing way.

questions.question: How does beautification function as a sign in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that creation is not only useful but also intentionally adorned.

questions.question: What does the reference to order from galaxies to fruits suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the same organizing wisdom governs both the largest and smallest realms.

questions.question: What does assigning duties to created things imply about the universe?
questions.answer: It implies that creation operates under purpose, direction, and responsibility rather than chance.

questions.question: Why does the passage call this testimony the second wing?
questions.answer: Because it is presented as one major supporting side of the cosmos’s overall witness.

questions.question: What truth does the passage say can be observed among beings in the world?
questions.answer: It says that beings show a real pattern of mutual support and working together.

questions.question: What two aims of creatures are mentioned at the start?
questions.answer: Their aims are to continue existing and, if alive, to maintain life and perform their tasks.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the world’s condition by mentioning ongoing changes and upheavals?
questions.answer: It implies that the world is unstable in itself and constantly shifting.

questions.question: Why is orderly co-operation during continual change a strong sign in the passage?
questions.answer: Because stable coordination in unstable conditions points to deliberate governance.

questions.question: What sequence of service is described from lower levels to higher ones?
questions.answer: Physical elements serve living things, clouds serve plants, plants serve animals, and animals serve humans.

questions.question: How does the feeding of a baby serve as evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows tender care reaching a creature that cannot provide for itself.

questions.question: Why is the source of provision described as unexpected?
questions.answer: To show that provision is sent by a higher giver, not secured by the recipient alone.

questions.question: What inner bodily process is mentioned to deepen the argument?
questions.answer: The delivery of nourishment to the body’s cells is mentioned.

questions.question: What does this cellular example reveal about the scale of divine care?
questions.answer: It reveals that care extends even to tiny hidden processes inside the body.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude from all these forms of support?
questions.answer: It concludes that they show the compassionate lordship of the One who sustains all worlds.

questions.question: What does the phrase about administering the cosmos like a palace emphasize?
questions.answer: It emphasizes disciplined management, arrangement, and oversight.

questions.question: Why is the behavior of inanimate things especially important for the passage’s reasoning?
questions.answer: Because if even unconscious things serve wisely, their service must come from a commander beyond them.

questions.question: Which divine qualities are especially connected to directing these lifeless things?
questions.answer: Mercy, wisdom, glory, power, and command are especially connected to that direction.

questions.question: What broad pattern is said to appear from planets down to tiny body parts?
questions.answer: A pattern of balanced measure and careful preservation appears at every level.

questions.question: How is beautification shown in both the heavens and the earth?
questions.answer: The sky, the earth, and flowers are all described as displaying intentional adornment.

questions.question: What does the mention of star systems and fruits together prove in the argument?
questions.answer: It proves that order is universal and not limited to either the very great or the very small.

questions.question: How do bees fit into the passage’s final list of examples?
questions.answer: They are an example of creatures carrying out specific assigned roles.

questions.question: What kind of testimony do all these truths offer?
questions.answer: They offer a witness whose strength matches the greatness of the realities being described.

questions.question: How does the passage end this discussion?
questions.answer: It says only a brief indication has been given because this testimony has been explained elsewhere.

questions.question: What is the passage asking the reader to notice first about the world?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to notice a deep pattern of co-operation among created things.

questions.question: What does the passage say living beings are trying to do?
questions.answer: They are trying to survive, stay alive, and fulfill their roles.

questions.question: Why is it important that this happens during continual change?
questions.answer: It shows that harmony is being maintained despite unstable conditions.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying this co-operation is beyond the beings’ capacities?
questions.answer: It means the creatures themselves do not have enough independent power or knowledge to produce such total coordination.

questions.question: How do the elements contribute to the system described?
questions.answer: They provide support for living beings.

questions.question: What service do clouds provide in this system?
questions.answer: They assist the growth and life of plants.

questions.question: How are plants and animals linked in the passage?
questions.answer: Plants are presented as helping animals, and animals as helping humans.

questions.question: What emotional tone is created by the example of milk for a baby?
questions.answer: It creates a tone of tenderness, mercy, and protective care.

questions.question: What larger point is made by examples of creatures receiving sustenance from unexpected places?
questions.answer: The point is that provision comes through divine care rather than through self-sufficiency alone.

questions.question: Why is the body’s nourishment system included among the examples?
questions.answer: To show that cooperation and directed service exist even at the microscopic level.

questions.question: What does all this reveal about the Sustainer’s relationship to the cosmos?
questions.answer: It reveals that the Sustainer actively governs it with mercy and care.

questions.question: Why is the image of a palace stronger than the image of a random field?
questions.answer: Because a palace suggests planning, order, administration, and purposeful arrangement.

questions.question: What argument is made from the fact that lifeless things work together in fitting ways?
questions.answer: The argument is that they must be made to do so by a wise and merciful ruler.

questions.question: Why can’t unconscious objects be the true source of this coordinated aid?
questions.answer: Because they lack awareness, intention, and independent wisdom.

questions.question: What does equilibrium contribute to the overall testimony of the cosmos?
questions.answer: It shows measured harmony and consistency across creation.

questions.question: What does preservation suggest about how the world is managed?
questions.answer: It suggests careful maintenance, not neglect or chaos.

questions.question: How does adornment support the passage’s message?
questions.answer: It shows that creation is fashioned with beauty and refinement, not bare utility alone.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by pairing the Milky Way with fruits?
questions.answer: It teaches that the same ordering wisdom appears in both immense and ordinary things.

questions.question: What is shown by saying duties are assigned from heavenly bodies down to bees?
questions.answer: It is shown that every level of creation has purposeful tasks under one rule.

questions.question: What final theological role does this whole discussion play?
questions.answer: It serves as the second major line of evidence in the universe’s witness to its Creator.

questions.question: What major reality does the passage present as visible in creation?
questions.answer: It presents a visible reality of widespread co-operation among beings.

questions.question: In the passage, what are creatures surrounded by while they strive to continue?
questions.answer: They are surrounded by ongoing changes and upheavals.

questions.question: What is the significance of saying this co-operation lies beyond their capacities?
questions.answer: It means the order cannot be fully explained by the creatures themselves.

questions.question: What pattern of assistance begins with the elements?
questions.answer: The pattern begins with basic physical things helping living creatures and continues upward through the rest of creation.

questions.question: How are clouds portrayed in relation to the plant world?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as helpers that serve vegetation.

questions.question: How are plants portrayed in relation to animals?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as a means of support and nourishment for animals.

questions.question: How are animals portrayed in relation to human beings?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as serving human benefit and life.

questions.question: What does the example of a mother feeding her child suggest about mercy?
questions.answer: It suggests direct and compassionate care for the vulnerable.

questions.question: What does receiving provision from unexpected sources imply about dependence?
questions.answer: It implies that creatures depend on a giver beyond themselves.

questions.question: How does the movement of nourishment to body cells support the main argument?
questions.answer: It shows precise service and regulation at an inner level that the cells themselves do not direct independently.

questions.question: What does the collection of these examples prove according to the passage?
questions.answer: It proves a universal and merciful lordship over the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What idea is communicated by saying the cosmos is governed like a palace?
questions.answer: The idea is that the cosmos is run under careful authority and wise arrangement.

questions.question: Why does the passage draw attention to the fact that inanimate objects are unfeeling?
questions.answer: To underline that their beneficial coordination must come from an external commander.

questions.question: What must be true if lifeless things still rush to help one another?
questions.answer: They must be driven by the command, power, and mercy of the Sustainer.

questions.question: Which realities are grouped together as further signs after the examples of co-operation?
questions.answer: Balance, preservation, adornment, order, and assigned functions are grouped together.

questions.question: How does the passage show that balance is universal?
questions.answer: It traces balance from celestial bodies down to bodily organs and tiny particles.

questions.question: What does the mention of decorated heavens, earth, and flowers add to the discussion?
questions.answer: It adds the point that beauty in creation is also deliberate and meaningful.

questions.question: Why are both large systems and small fruits used as examples of order?
questions.answer: To demonstrate that order covers all scales of creation.

questions.question: What does assigning tasks to both cosmic bodies and small creatures reveal?
questions.answer: It reveals a single governing wisdom that directs every level of existence.

questions.question: What place does this testimony hold in the broader witness of the cosmos?
questions.answer: It forms the second wing of that witness.
